proposals.impact: reduce zero-start drop-off on quiz intro screen
proposals.observation: The quiz had 1 session and 0 starts in the 48-hour window. The single visitor loaded the intro screen and left without pressing start. This is a conversion cliff at the very first interaction — no quiz data is being collected, no leads are entering the automation sequences, and the existing open-rate gains on Money Vigilance (66.67%) cannot compound if nobody reaches the profile-tagging step. The intro copy is the only plausible lever before the start button.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the quiz intro screen copy to reduce the gap between arriving and pressing start. The current text (see below) frames the quiz as a diagnostic tool with generic benefit language. It does not give the visitor a sensory reason to care in the first 10 seconds. Replace with copy that names the exact recognisable feeling the ICP carries into the page: earning well, spending fine, but nothing actually accumulating. Keep it to three short paragraphs. No list. No header hierarchy beyond the h1.
proposals.current_text:
Find out your Money Script and unlock personalised insights into your financial behaviour.

This short quiz takes around 5 minutes to complete. Answer honestly — there are no right or wrong answers.

Your results will help you understand the hidden patterns shaping your financial decisions.
proposals.new_text:
You earn enough. You're not reckless. But at the end of most months, you open your banking app and feel a quiet dread you can't quite name.

This 5-minute quiz identifies the specific money script driving that pattern — the story beneath the spending, the saving, the not-quite-looking.

Answer honestly. The results will be accurate to the degree you are.

proposals.impact: lift Money Worship open rate to match Vigilance baseline
proposals.observation: Money Worship is the weakest automation by open rate at 37.5%, sitting 29 percentage points below Money Vigilance (66.67%) with a comparable send volume (16 vs 12). The subject line is the most likely cause because automation body content is not surfaced in the data. A single subject-line edit is a one-field change in the sequence config file and can be A/B-tested within the next send cycle.
proposals.proposal: Replace the subject line on email 1 of the Money Worship automation. The current subject line reads as a category label rather than a felt experience. People who score Money Worship often believe more money will solve the discomfort, so the subject line needs to meet them at that belief rather than naming it from the outside. Write to the specific Saturday-morning feeling of checking a account that's grown and still feeling nothing settle.
proposals.current_text: Subject: Your Money Worship results are ready
proposals.new_text: Subject: You got more. Why doesn't it feel like enough?

proposals.observation: Two CI workflows failed in the last 24 hours: Daily Blog Post (08:41 UTC) and Funnel-Hack Digest (13:52 UTC). The blog post failure is higher priority because the content queue shows only 1 post queued against 47 published — the pipeline is the only thing keeping daily publishing alive, and a second consecutive failure tomorrow would create a visible gap on the blog index. The workflow file needs inspection; the most common cause at this stack level is an expired API key or a changed environment variable name following a dependency update.
proposals.proposal: Open the Daily Blog Post workflow file and check the environment variable references against the current repository secrets list. The failure timestamp (08:41 UTC) predates the two cursor-update commits, so the fault is not a merge conflict. Add a explicit `env` block validation step before the main job runs, so future failures surface a clear error message rather than a silent exit code. This is a one-block addition to the workflow YAML — adding a preflight job that echoes masked secret presence without exposing values.
proposals.current_text:
jobs:
  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
proposals.new_text:
jobs:
  preflight:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Confirm required secrets are present
        run: |
          missing=0
          for var in OPENAI_API_KEY MAILERLITE_API_KEY GITHUB_TOKEN; do
            if [ -z "${!var}" ]; then
              echo "MISSING: $var"
              missing=1
            else
              echo "OK: $var is set"
            fi
          done
          [ $missing -eq 0 ] || exit 1
        env:
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          MAILERLITE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.MAILERLITE_API_KEY }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
  publish:
    needs: preflight
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
